text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Lennart Meri met the Emperor of Japan Akihito and invited him to visit Estonia.
- Estonia and Sweden exchanged diplomatic notes on visa-free travel from May 1. Visa-free travel with Finland will be signed today in Tallinn and with Norway on April 7, officials said.
- Three politicians who wanted to bring Meri to trial, saying he lied in his oath office by saying he did not work for the KGB, have not given up their fight but are looking for evidence in Russia.
- The postponement of the Estonian-Russian border agreement should not be an obstacle to Estonia's aims for European Union membership, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said.
- The government approved Estonia's forestry policy, intended to preserve forests and supervise their use.
- There will be no queues for phone connection in Estonia in four years time, leaders of the company Eesti Telefon promise in their business plan for 1997-2006.
- Parliament postponed for three months the debate of whether to hold a poll on the Estonian-Russian border.
- Parliament is debating a new excise law which would differentiate excise rates on beer. The new regime would favor small breweries, the director of Saku Brewery in Tallinn said.
